newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-HIGHLANDERS DOWN N.TRANSVAAL IN NZ.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-HIGHLANDERS DOWN N.TRANSVAAL IN NZ.

text.p: The Otago Highlanders put on an improved display of attacking rugby mixed with stout defence to beat the Northern Transvaal Blue Bulls 27-7 in a Super 12 match at Carisbrook on Saturday.
It was the Highlanders' first win of the series and their performance dispelled any doubts about their commitment following heavy losses to Natal and Transvaal in South Africa.

The Blue Bulls started well, testing the home team from the outset with some ferocious mauling, before overzealous play by lock Johan Otto resulted in his being sin-binned just three minutes into the match.
Another error from the visitors two minutes later saw Highlanders fly-half Simon Culhane kick the first of his five penalties from a handy position.

During the next 10 minutes, as the South Africans continued to make mistakes in the face of some powerful Otago play, Culhane landed two more penalties to open up a 9-0 lead, helped by Northern Transvaal's Dirkie Nortje failing with his two penalty attempts.

The Highlanders crossed for the first of their two tries after 22 minutes when right winger Pailate Fili, making his Super 12 debut, crossed wide out after excellent buildup work from the forwards and quick hands among the inside backs.

Culhane added the conversion for a 16-0 lead but five minutes later Northern Transvaal kept themselves in the match when captain and flanker Ruben Kruger neatly ran on to a pass in midfield to split the Otago backline on the 22m line and cross between the posts race unimpeded.
Nortje added the conversion to make the score 16-7 although Culhane kicked another penalty eight minutes from the break to give the Highlanders a 19-7 lead.

The All Blacks reserve fly-half landed his fifth penalty shortly after the break and while Northern Transvaal lifted their performance during the second half, wrong options and too many handling mistakes saw most of that good work wasted.
With time running out and the visitors completely devoid of new attacking ideas, left winger Jeff Wilson put the game beyond reach by intercepting a poor pass and racing 40m to score in the corner.

Northern Transvaal coach Uli Schmidt praised Otago for their tremendous courage on defence. However, he was still confident his side could make the semi-finals despite losing both their matches in New Zealand in the past week.
"I think we will still end up in the top four. We just have get one or two problems sorted out and we'll be on the road again."

Otago Highlanders - Matthew Carrington, Pailate Fili, Romi Ropati, John Leslie, Jeff Wilson; Simon Culhane, Stu Forster; Isitolo Maka; Taine Randell (captain), Lio Falaniko, Simon Maling, Steve Gordon; Kees Meeuws, Anton Oliver, Carl Hoeft.

Northern Transvaal - Clive Terreblanche, Nicholas Alberts, Danie Van Schalkwyk, Wynward Lourens; Kosie Van Vuuren, Dirkie Nortje; Conrad Breytenbach; Schutte Bekker, Ruben Kruger (captain), Nicky Van der Walt; Wium Basson, Johan Otto; Frikkie Bosman, Henry Tromp, Pierre Ribbens.
